title: Security questionnaire effort tracking and price-credit calibration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Enterprise RFPs and security questionnaires (SIG/CAIQ and bespoke vendor forms) are a growing operational cost. Sales and Solutions teams log multi-day engagements to satisfy a single deal, with no consistent way to capture hours or to convert that cost into pricing credits or a paid service.

Goal: Run a lightweight experiment to (1) instrument and measure the true engineering and solutions effort to respond to security questionnaires, (2) build a defensible pricing credit / surcharge model that compensates for heavy attestation work, and (3) prototype an opt-in paid Attestation Service + self-serve credits flow in Console.

Success metrics: (a) Accurate time-per-questionnaire baseline for 90% of inbound requests (target average: +/- 20% variance), (b) Proposal for credit pricing that recovers >= 70% of labor cost over pilot customers, (c) One Console mock/prototype and 2 pilot customers contract the paid flow within 8 weeks.

Scope and approach:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Instrumentation & intake changes: update Zendesk intake form to capture questionnaire type (SIG/CAIQ/custom), number of questions, requester org size, and whether answers can be drawn from existing Answer Library. Add time-tracking template for Solutions/Eng/Legal to log effort per request.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): Data collection & analysis: collect 20 responses minimum across small/medium/enterprise customers. Classify effort buckets: <2h (quick), 2-8h (moderate), 8-40h (high), >40h (bespoke). Calculate blended hourly rate (fully burdened) for RBC cost modeling.
- Phase 3 (3 weeks): Pricing credit model design: define two options (credits-as-allowance bundled with enterprise plans; a la carte paid Attestation Service). Model revenue/recovery scenarios and customer objections.
- Phase 4 (4 weeks): Prototype console flow + legal/SME-run pilot: small UX in Console to request paid attestation and to consume credits; legal/solutions deliver to pilot customers.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Risk: Charging for attestation could slow enterprise sales motion; mitigation: offer initial free allowance tied to committed spend, and provide clear SLAs for paid service.
- Operational overhead: Time-tracking imposes friction; mitigate by providing a simple clipboard-style logging sheet and Slack slash command for quick capture.
- Productization timeline: Full self-serve credits requires Console and billing work; pilot can use manual invoice/credit offsets to validate price sensitivity faster.

Data and instrumentation checklist:
- Zendesk intake form update (field names and dropdowns).
- Internal time log Google Sheet + Slack / Notion template for engineers and solutions.
- Dashboard in Amplitude or Looker showing count, average hours, distribution by questionnaire type.

Stakeholders and approvers:
- PM lead: Priya Kapoor (owner), Creator/SME: Ava Chen
- Sales lead: Marcus Rivera
- Legal/Compliance SME: Elena Martínez
- Solutions Eng lead: Noah Patel
- Finance: Charlotte Nguyen (cost model review)

Deliverables:
- Measured baseline report (10–20 sample responses) with effort buckets and proposed credit ranges.
- Pricing calibration memo for Sales to include in proposal playbooks.
- Console prototype wireframe and an internal request + manual billing flow for pilot.

Acceptance criteria:
- Instrumentation capturing questionnaire metadata on >= 80% of inbound requests.
- Baseline report delivered and reviewed by Sales + Legal.
- Pricing memo with 2 concrete options (bundle allowance and a la carte) and recommended implementation path.

Long-term vision: If validated, fold Attestation Service into the product suite as a billable add-on with tiered allowances and automation (re-use answer library, contract templates, response SLAs).
